lines.text: Task five. Your agent is still carrying everything from tasks one through four.
That is slow, because it re-reads everything. Expensive, because you pay for all of it.
The fix is simple. Every task should start fresh, as if it were the first job of the day.
A task finishes. The code is committed and the result is reported.
Agent R Q sends slash clear to the Claude Code agent right before it picks up the next task.
The next task starts with an empty context. Fix the signup email bug.
Anything worth keeping lives in workspace memory, so the agent loads the notes and not the noise.
Without stale context to re-read, the agent answers faster on every turn.
It spends fewer tokens too, so you pay for the task, not the history.
And it stays on topic, with no bleed from the last task into the new one.
All of it happens automatically, before every task, with nothing for you to remember.
How much of your agent budget goes to old context? Drop your story below, and try clear context at Agent R Q dot com.
